sources.entry: fiftyone - The open-source tool for building high-quality datasets and computer vision models.

summary.one_liner: FiftyOne is an open-source Python tool for visualizing, labeling, evaluating, and curating image and video datasets for computer vision and visual AI models.
summary.what_it_does: FiftyOne lets you explore images, videos, and their associated labels through a visual App launched from Python. You can create and edit 2D and 3D labels directly in the App or connect external annotation tools. It supports evaluating model performance, identifying failure modes, and exploring data through embeddings by selecting points and viewing the matching samples. It includes data curation features for finding and fixing data issues, annotation errors, and edge cases. The README says it integrates with libraries such as PyTorch, Hugging Face, and Ultralytics, and it includes a dataset zoo with a quickstart dataset.
use_cases: find failure modes in a model
curate datasets and fix annotation errors
how_to_run: In scripts, call session.wait() to keep the App open
notable: Interactive App for exploring and labeling datasets in the browser
Embeddings exploration to view samples behind selected points
Integrates with FiftyOne Brain and a model zoo, per the README's resource list
Source install script builds the App
caveats: Source installs require Node.js, Yarn, and a build of the App
Video work needs a separate FFmpeg install
Production-grade cloud collaboration is offered through the separate Voxel51 product
